content: 1. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and NSAIDs: Co-administration of this combination with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs (e.g., diflunisal) may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. This is because both drugs are primarily excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion. Alternative therapies to NSAIDs should be considered, and renal function should be closely monitored. 2. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Digoxin: Cobicistat inhibits P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transport, leading to increased digoxin levels. Initiate digoxin at a low dose and titrate carefully while monitoring for toxicity. 3. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Dihydroergotamine/Ergotamine: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, which significantly increases plasma concentrations of ergot derivatives. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events. 4. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Diltiazem: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing diltiazem levels. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering calcium channel blockers with this regimen. 5. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Disopyramide: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, leading to increased disopyramide levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 6. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Docetaxel: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing docetaxel levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Doxepin: Cobicistat inhibits CYP2D6, increasing doxepin levels. Use caution with CYP2D6 substrates, as elevated plasma concentrations may lead to serious or life-threatening events. 8. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Dronabinol: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing dronabinol levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Edoxaban: Cobicistat inhibits P-glycoprotein, increasing edoxaban levels. Dose adjustments may be required. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 10. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Efavirenz: Efavirenz induces CYP3A4, reducing the levels of elvitegravir. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. 11. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Enasidenib: Avoid co-administration with enasidenib due to its effects on OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates, which may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 12. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Eszopiclone: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing eszopiclone levels. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day and monitor closely. 13. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ethinyl Estradiol: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing ethinyl estradiol levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide induces CYP3A4, reducing elvitegravir levels. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. 15. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Erythromycin: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing erythromycin levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 16. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Escitalopram: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing escitalopram levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 17. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Eslicarbazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing elvitegravir levels. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. 18. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Estazolam: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing estazolam levels. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 19. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing elbasvir/grazoprevir levels. Avoid co-administration due to the risk of serious toxicities. 20. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Elagolix: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing elagolix levels. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 21. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Encorafenib: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, increasing encorafenib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. 22. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Entecavir: Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ergot Alkaloids: Cobicistat inhibits CYP3A4, significantly increasing ergot alkaloid levels. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events.
